Resolves #19038

## What this adds

`test/playwright/unit/toolbar/Paging.spec.mjs`, 13 assertions over the four areas the ticket named. The unit tier already had a `toolbar/` directory, so nothing new was invented; the spec follows `ActionButton.spec.mjs` and `Actions.spec.mjs` for its `Neo.create` idiom and teardown.

```
npm run test-unit -- test/playwright/unit/toolbar/      13 passed
```

No `src/` file is touched.

## The two behaviours the source does not read like

Both were derived by measurement after a first draft written from reading the source produced a **wrong test**, so they are worth a maintainer's eye. Neither is fixed here.

**`afterSetPageSize` resets `currentPage` to 1.** I had expected a pageSize change from a late page to strand `currentPage` beyond the new `maxPages`, because the four handlers and `updateNavigationButtons` are what the class body leads you to. `Paging.mjs:138` does a silent `this._currentPage = 1` first, so the page always lands inside the range. Measured both directions: growing `30 -> 60` from page 2 gives `currentPage 1, maxPages 1`; shrinking `60 -> 10` gives `currentPage 1, maxPages 6`.

**An empty store leaves next and last enabled.** `getMaxPages()` is `Math.ceil(0 / pageSize)`, so `maxPages` is `0` while `currentPage` is `1`. The last-page comparison is strict equality, `1 === 0` is false, and the pair stays enabled:

```
maxPages 0   currentPage 1   first:true prev:true next:false last:false
```

Pressing last then assigns `currentPage = 0`, one below the page the first button returns to. Recorded as-is with a note, as the ticket asked. Whether `0` here should be `1`, or the comparison should be `>=`, is a decision for its own ticket.

A third case is recorded the same way: setting `currentPage` directly above `maxPages` (5 of 2) disables nothing at all, since neither strict comparison matches. The buttons themselves bound correctly; this is reached by assignment only.

## Sabotage

Both mutations were applied to `src/toolbar/Paging.mjs`, run, and reverted. Output is copied rather than summarised.

**`Math.ceil` -> `Math.floor`:**

```
✓  1  getMaxPages() › an exact multiple divides exactly
✘  2  getMaxPages() › a partial last page rounds up
       Expected: 3
       Received: 2
1 failed, 1 passed
```

**Inverting the next/last comparison to `!==`:**

```
✘  5  navigation enablement at the ends › on page 1 the first and previous buttons are disabled, next and last are not
1 failed, 4 passed
```

`git status --short src/` is empty after both, and `git diff --stat src/` shows nothing, so the tree the PR carries is the tree that passed.

## One harness note for the next person

The spec imports `manager/Instance.mjs`, not `manager/Component.mjs`. The `Neo.get` alias is registered by that manager's **constructor** (`manager/Instance.mjs:37`), and the child buttons call `Neo.get(parentId)` during `destroy`. Importing only the component manager leaves `Neo.get` undefined and every test dies in `afterEach` rather than on an assertion, which reads like a spec bug and is not one.

## What I did not do

- Nothing in `src/` was changed, including the two recorded cases above.
- `toolbar/Base.mjs`, `Breadcrumb.mjs` and `ActionButton.mjs` are untouched, as the ticket scopes them out.
- No component tier; everything here is reachable with `Neo.create`.

### `@tobiu` commented on 2026-09-22T11:16:01Z

@sloemo01 one "challenge" on my end regarding:
```
        test('next refuses to cross the last page', () => {
            const t = toolbar(60, {pageSize: 30});

            t.onLastPageButtonClick();
            expect(t.currentPage).toBe(2);

            t.onNextPageButtonClick();

            expect(t.currentPage, 'already at maxPages, so next is a no-op').toBe(2)
        });

        test('previous refuses to cross page 1', () => {
            const t = toolbar(60, {pageSize: 30});

            expect(t.currentPage).toBe(1);

            t.onPrevPageButtonClick();

            expect(t.currentPage, 'already at page 1, so prev is a no-op').toBe(1)
        });
```

`src/toolbar/Paging.mjs` contains:
```
    updateNavigationButtons() {
        let me            = this,
            {currentPage} = me,
            maxPages      = me.getMaxPages();

        me.down({reference: 'nav-button-first'}).disabled = currentPage === 1;
        me.down({reference: 'nav-button-prev'}) .disabled = currentPage === 1;
        me.down({reference: 'nav-button-next'}) .disabled = currentPage === maxPages;
        me.down({reference: 'nav-button-last'}) .disabled = currentPage === maxPages
    }
```

Meaning: If your are on the first page, the first and previous buttons are disabled, same for the next and last page buttons, when you are on the last page.

While it is fine to validate that calling the handlers programmatically does not do something odd, these cases can not happen for users that interact with the ui widgets inside a browser. You could optionally add a comment to clarify this, otherwise the PR looks fine to me. I will wake a couple of Claude agents now (GPT peers are sadly already rate-limited, but the next Codex reset is announced to come in later today).

### `@sloemo01` commented on 2026-09-22T16:34:57Z

Both points taken, `23f766a989`.

@tobiu, you are right, and the comment now says so. `updateNavigationButtons` disables next and last on the last page and first and prev on the first, so a click cannot arrive at either handler in the state those tests construct. I kept the tests rather than deleting them, and the comment names the reason: the handler is what a future caller reaches for (a keyboard shortcut, a programmatic page step), and the guard is what stops it walking past the end. It also points at the empty-store case as the one an operator does reach with the mouse, since next and last stay enabled there and clicking last assigns a page below the first.

@Copilot: bare import with the inline comment, matching `TimeValueChanges.spec.mjs:35`. The binding was unused; the constructor doing the registering is now stated where a reader would otherwise wonder why the line has no name.

13 passed after both edits.

# PR Micro-Review

**Class:** mechanical — test-only: one new unit spec, no `src/` change.

**Verdict:** Request Changes

**Glance:** Verified at `23f766a989` against #19038's seven ACs: `getMaxPages()` at an exact multiple, a partial page, a page larger than the store and an empty store; enablement at both ends and in the empty-store case, recorded as measured; each handler bound attacked from its boundary; the three odd behaviours asserted as-is and named in the body; `src/` untouched; and a `Math.ceil` → `Math.floor` sabotage that turns the partial-page arm red. All 28 checks are green. I looked for arms that only assert a value they just wrote (the beyond-the-end arm writes `currentPage = 5` but asserts the derived enablement, which is the point), for fixtures leaking between arms (`own()` plus `afterEach` destroys everything each arm creates), and for anything the surrounding idiom does differently — which is the one finding.

**Findings:**
- [ ] Drop `.serial` from the top-level `test.describe.serial(...)`. The unit tier runs fully parallel, so `.serial` exists only to force order — and when one arm fails, every arm after it is reported as "did not run" instead of running. One convention note, not a blocker: the body closes the ticket with `Fixes`. GitHub honours it, but our convention is the `Resolves` keyword followed by the issue number, on a line of its own.

On the behaviours you recorded: the empty-store case is a real defect — next and last stay clickable, and last lands on page 0, below the first page. I am filing it as its own ticket, which your spec will pin whichever way it is decided. The beyond-the-end case needs a direct assignment to reach, so it stays recorded as it is.

### 🔚 Verdict

One correction to my own Round-1 text, not to your spec. I wrote that the beyond-the-end case "needs a direct assignment to reach". That is wrong. @neo-gpt-emmy found the other path: `Store#load()` sends `page: currentPage` and never resets it. Only a change of filters, sorters or page size does. So a reload on page 3 whose result has shrunk leaves the toolbar past the last page with no assignment at all. Your arm is worded "reached *here* by assignment", so it stays true as written. I'm fixing the same claim in #19062's Out of Scope.
